name: Digital Detox
tagline: 60 days to break the scroll and reclaim your attention.
description: A neuroscience-based 60-day program to beat phone, social media, and screen addiction — kill the notification-dopamine loop, restore your attention span, and rebuild an analog life you actually enjoy.

phases.label: P1
phases.title: Breaking the Cycle
phases.vibe: The first two weeks strip the hooks: kill notifications, grayscale the screen, and keep the phone out of the bedroom. Each buzz was a tiny dopamine hit training you to check. Remove the cue and the loop starves.

phases.label: P2
phases.title: Rewiring the Brain
phases.vibe: Your thumb still reaches for the phone at the old moments — give those moments a better routine. A book, a walk, a real conversation. You're rebuilding an attention span that endless feeds deliberately fractured.

phases.label: P3
phases.title: Building a New Identity
phases.vibe: You're now someone who uses tech on purpose, not on reflex. Deep focus, real presence, and boredom tolerance are yours again. You design a life the feed can't compete with.

0.title: No phone for the first hour
0.note: Wake without the scroll. Water, light, one intention. Starting on your own terms protects your attention before the feed hijacks it.

0.title: Kill non-essential notifications
0.note: Turn off badges and alerts for social/news. Each ping is an engineered dopamine cue — remove the cue, break the loop.

0.title: Grayscale + tidy home screen
0.note: Set the screen to grayscale and hide addictive apps off page one. Color and one-tap access are designed to pull you back; friction reduces use.

0.title: 20 min screen-free movement
0.note: Walk without headphones or leave the phone home. Movement gives real dopamine and lets a restless mind settle.

0.title: Pause before you unlock
0.note: Before opening a feed, take one breath and ask 'why?'. Inserting a gap between cue and action is how you regain control of the impulse.

0.title: 30 min analog activity
0.note: Read a paper book, cook, draw, play music. Rebuilds the sustained-attention circuits infinite scroll erodes.

0.title: Phone out of the bedroom
0.note: Charge it in another room; use a real alarm. Blue light and late scrolling wreck sleep and morning willpower.

0.title: Evening journal — screen-time review
0.note: Check your screen-time number and note one trigger. Awareness of the real number is a powerful corrective.

1.title: Phone-free morning routine
1.note: Extend the phone-free window. The longer you protect the morning, the sharper the whole day.

1.title: Run your scroll-replacement
1.note: When you'd normally scroll (line, break, couch), do your swap: read, stretch, breathe. Same cue, new routine.

1.title: 45 min single-task focus
1.note: Phone in another room, one task, no tabs. Deep work rebuilds the attention span that apps fragmented.

1.title: 30 min movement
1.note: Screen-free exercise. Real-world dopamine makes the digital kind less tempting.

1.title: One real, in-person/voice talk
1.note: Call or meet someone — no texting. Face-to-face contact delivers the connection social media only simulates.

1.title: Sit with 10 min of boredom
1.note: No input — just be. Tolerating boredom rebuilds impulse control and sparks real creativity.

1.title: Reflect + set tomorrow's limits
1.note: Review usage and set app limits for tomorrow. Pre-commitment beats in-the-moment willpower.

2.title: Intentional morning
2.note: Wake, move, plan — screens wait. This is simply how you live now.

2.title: 60-90 min deep work
2.note: Long, undistracted focus is your superpower again. Guard it fiercely.

2.title: Train — your standard now
2.note: Movement anchors a low-stimulation, high-energy life.

2.title: Create, don't just consume
2.note: Write, build, make something. Producing rewires you from passive feed to active life.

2.title: Real-world connection
2.note: People over profiles. Presence is the whole point.

2.title: Identity journal
2.note: Write as a focused, present person. Self-image steers behavior.

2.title: Phone out, wind down
2.note: Analog evenings, deep sleep. Protect the reset.

quotes: Your attention is the most valuable thing you own. Stop giving it away for free.
The urge to check is a wave — let it pass unclicked.
Boredom is where creativity is born.
You don't need a longer feed. You need a fuller life.
Every notification you kill is attention you keep.
The apps were built to hook you. Unhooking is a skill you can learn.
Presence is a superpower in a distracted world.
Sixty days off the slot machine and your mind comes back.
